content:
OK, please follow these instructions:

• in Thunderbird go to Settings > General > scroll to bottom and click "Config Editor...", search for toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets and toggle its value from false to true • open a text editor and copy + paste the following CSS code in the editor 

#item-description {  background-color: #E6E6FA !important; }


• name the file userChrome.css , save it to your Desktop and remove the .txt suffixe your OS will add • create a folder, name it chrome and move the userChrome.css file in folder chrome • in Thunderbird go to Help >Troubleshooting Information > Profile Folder > Open Folder...., then exit Thunderbird • move the folder chrome in the profile folder and restart Thunderbird

Instead of the "lavender" background color you can choose the color you prefer here https://cloford.com/resources/colours/500col.htm Just replace #E6E6FA (lavender) with the hexadecimal code of the color of your choice.

Do I understand you correctly, that people who are trying to send email to you are receiving this error message? It usually means that their sending (SMTP) server is not responding. It's usually temporary, but could indicate more serious problems on the server end. If I'm misunderstanding, please clarify.

If YOU are seeing this error message while trying to send a message, it suggests that either Spectrum's servers are not working properly or you have wrong server settings in Thunderbird.

I'm not clear about what esmerise.com has to do with it, unless it's their sending servers that are malfunctioning.

If Spectrum is involved, it's very possible that they are having server troubles and either won't admit it, or their support people don't know about it. They have been having unresolved intermittent problems for months.

content:
Beyond drag and drop there is another workaround.

  • At the top right of the Thunderbird window, click the menu button ≡ > Settings > General
  • Scroll down to the bottom and click 'Config Editor'.
  • Search for the preference mail.compose.attach.dir.
  • The value (Path) here must be changed to one that is still available (for example C:).
  • Restart Thunderbird.

That should fix it.
